newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Spending cuts amount to new Russia budget - Shokhin.
newsitem.headline: Spending cuts amount to new Russia budget - Shokhin.

text.p: Spending cuts which the Russian government is expected to make in April will in effect amount to a new 1997 budget, Alexander Shokhin, first deputy speaker of the State Duma lower house of parliament, said on Thursday.
"The budget crisis we're dealing with now is raising the question of introducing a new budget -- not just sequestering unprotected parts of the budget," Shokhin told a news conference.

Communists make up the largest faction in the Duma and Shokhin, himself a member of the government party Our Home is Russia, said deputies might fight efforts to reduce spending or suggest printing money to pay for services.
"One cannot rule out that, in the course of that discussion, people will think about proposing a vote of no confidence in the government," he said.
Communist Party leader Gennady Zyuganov has already said the communists will not back proposals to cut spending.

Ministers say the cuts will be needed because tax collection is running well below schedule and the budget says the government must submit revised spending plans to parliament if tax revenues fall below 90 percent of targeted levels.

Shokhin said tax receipts were so low the government would have to reduce financing for so-called "unprotected" budget items to 20 percent of planned levels if financing for protected items remained in place.
"That's in effect a new budget, although it will be passed through the sequestration scheme," he said.

"Simply lowering financing is very difficult. We'll have to cut funding for some things completely to keep funding at levels of say 45 percent for those things which, although not protected, are nevertheless important."
Russia's budget includes so-called "protected items", including spending on health, education and the military.
The head of the Duma's tax committee said earlier this week that these items could be at risk under sequestration plans.

Shokhin, giving the latest in a chain of different figures from different officials, said tax receipts were only 60 percent of target and the government should propose changing the tax system to boost revenues as part of its sequestration package.
The government is due to submit the final details of the its new tax code to the Duma by the end of April, but approval is expected to take at least a year.
Some deputies have proposed passing elements of the code as separate laws to speed the process, and Shokhin said some parts of the code could come into effect that way by July 1.
"If we do that we have a chance of correcting the budget without issuing money," Shokhin said.
